# Abstract

This spec proposes a solution to use the ingress-configurator as the bridge between the haproxy charm and the content cache charm to tell haproxy to use the content cache as the backend instead of directly hitting the real backend.

# Rationale

In the [IS156 - Content Cache Service](https://docs.google.com/document/u/0/d/1LhUio2Wb7ImAXirF-f6gPwbhov5bRWKhbNWQDLUamzM/edit) spec, IS intends to use the content cache charm to provide caching and CDN for Canonical services. The exact details of the deployment architecture have not been finalized yet, but it is necessary to have a relation between the haproxy charm, the content cache charm, and the ingress requirer charm to tell haproxy to use the content cache as the backend instead of directly hitting the real backend.

# Specification

## **Ingress-configurator as glue:**

In this solution, the ingress requirer charm will first integrate with the ingress-configurator charm. Then the ingress-configurator charm will be integrated with the content cache charm and the haproxy charm.

The ingress-configurator charm will extract the backend information from the configuration and the ingress relation, mainly the backend address information, and pass it to the content cache charm via the cache-config relation. The content cache charm should then allocate a unique port for this backend and return the unique port and IP address of the content cache unit through the cache-config relation. Returning a unique port for each different backend means that the content cache charm will not need to perform host/path-based routing, as that is already done by the haproxy charm. This feature does not exist in the current version of the content cache charm.

Once the ingress-configurator charm has received the content cache IP and port in the cache-config relation, the ingress-configurator will replace the backend address in the haproxy\_route relation with the content cache address. Then the ingress-configurator will pass the modified haproxy\_route relation to haproxy.

Haproxy will receive the haproxy\_route relation data, where the backend address in the haproxy\_route relation has been replaced with the content cache address instead of the real backend address. Thus, the haproxy charm will communicate with the content cache and serve the cached result instead of directly hitting the real backend.

## **HTTPS backend**

The backend might use the HTTPS protocol to ensure data integrity and encryption. To use an HTTPS backend, certificate trust needs to be set up on the content-cache and HAProxy charms to make it function properly. We will use the existing certificate\_transfer relation for this purpose.

### **Certificate and TLS termination**

When the content-cache charm is set up to provide caching for an HTTPS backend, the content-cache must terminate and decrypt the HTTPS requests coming from the HAProxy charm in order to cache the response. Thus, when using an HTTPS backend, there should be two sets of certificates. One certificate is used by the backend server for requests coming from the content-cache to the backend server (we will call this the backend certificate). The content-cache charm should also request a set of TLS certificates for requests coming from HAProxy to the content-cache charm (we will call this the cache certificate below).

For the HAProxy charm, it needs to know and trust the public part of the cache certificate. For the content-cache charm, it needs to know the private part of the cache certificate, and know and trust the public part of the backend certificate. For the backend charm, it needs to know the private part of the backend certificate.

Based on this premise, we can derive the following scheme. For the backend charm, we should deploy a TLS certificate provider charm, such as the lego charm (we will call it backend-lego below). The backend charm should integrate with the TLS certificate provider charm (backend-lego) using the tls-certificates relation to obtain the private part of the certificate. The same TLS certificate provider charm (backend-lego) will also integrate with the content-cache charm using the certificate\_transfer relation to provide the public part of the backend certificate to the content-cache charm.

For the content-cache charm, there will also be a TLS certificate provider charm, such as the lego charm (we will call it cache-lego below). The content-cache charm should integrate with the TLS certificate provider charm (cache-lego) using the tls-certificates relation, and the HAProxy charm will integrate with cache-lego using the certificate\_transfer relation.

## **In this way, all the necessary information for forming HTTPS connections is available between all components.**  **Implementation**

### **Modification of the content-cache charm**

#### **Remove hostname- and path-based routing**

The content-cache charm currently supports hostname- and path-based routing for incoming HTTP requests. This is error-prone when the content-cache is integrated with the HAProxy charm, as the HAProxy charm also performs hostname- and path-based routing, with the possibility of path rewriting.

Thus, the hostname- and path-based routing capability of the content-cache charm should be removed. Instead, the content-cache charm should allocate a unique port for each individual backend. When requests come to the port, the content-cache charm should just cache them and send them to the corresponding backend, with no hostname or path routing performed.

The related fields inside the cache-config relation, for example, hostname, path, and backend-path, should also be removed.

This change will break backward compatibility of the content-cache charm, but considering that the content-cache charm is not officially used, this is acceptable.

#### **Return cache-backends in the cache-config relation**

When the content-cache charm receives new backend information from the cache-config relation, it should return a cache-backends field to the requirer. The cache backend should be a list of URLs, for example, http://10.0.0.1:51251 and https://192.168.0.1:54243, denoting the content-cache address, the content-cache allocated port for this backend, and the protocol the content-cache is listening on. This information will be used by the ingress-configurator to replace the haproxy\_route before passing it to the upstream HAProxy charm.

#### **Support HTTPS backends**

The content-cache charm should support the certificate\_transfer relation and HTTPS backends using the certificates received from certificate\_transfer.

During the initial version, TLS server name validation can be turned off when connecting to the backend to simplify the implementation, similar to the HAProxy charm.

### **Modification of the ingress-configurator charm**

#### **Support cache-config relation**

The ingress-configurator should now support the cache-config relation. The ingress-configurator will first send the cache backend extracted from the ingress relation or from the ingress-configurator configuration to the content-cache charm integrated with the cache-config relation. Then the ingress-configurator will retrieve the cache-backends from the cache-config relation and use them to replace the backend information in the haproxy\_route relation before sending it to the upstream haproxy charm.

The ingress-configurator should also add cache relation configurations, for example, proxy\_cache\_valid.
